newsitem.title: USA: Babbitt to tour Alaskan National Petroleum Reserve.
newsitem.headline: Babbitt to tour Alaskan National Petroleum Reserve.

text.p: U.S. Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt next week plans to tour part of Alaska's National Petroleum Reserve (NPR-A), which the Clinton administration is considering opening to oil drilling, the Interior Department said Friday.

On the trip from July 7-11, Babbitt will meet with Alaskan officials, natives, scientific researchers and others interested in the planning and environmental assessment underway in the North Slope region.
"I come with an open mind, and I hope to leave this vast, undeveloped area with a greater understanding of the many complex decisions to be made in the future," he said in a statement.
"I view this as a unique firsthand opportunity to meet the people and see the wildlife habitat in a fragile and abundant landscape that all must depend upon for future benefit," he added.

The Bureau of Land Management plans to complete a study by next summer of the potential environmental impacts of oil and gas leasing in the northeast corner of the 23 million acre reserve, with an eye to offering leases possibly in 1998.
